mangin_first_order.what: Effective focal length of the collimator: ray-transfer matrices (thick Mangin mirror, first order) against the plate scale of the exact ray trace
mangin_first_order.note: The difference is the off-axis geometry: the emitter sits 8.3 degrees off the tube axis and the plate scale is measured in its plane; 1/cos^2 of that angle is the size of the effect.

thin_lens_parallax.what: Parallax error for 1 mm of eye offset: exact ray trace against the thin-lens relation e * (1/D - 1/D0)

dot_size.what: Angle between the traced images of the two edges of the emitter

collimation_along_the_axis.what: Largest change in the dot direction when the eye moves 100 mm nearer or farther (centre and 6 mm off axis)

window_see_through.what: Residual power of the doublet for the scene (it should be a zero-power window)

polynomial_fit.what: Order-5 polynomial of the beam direction against the ray trace over an 11.5 mm eye disc

published_parallax.what: Dot movement on the target as the eye sweeps edge to edge across the window, mean over 25, 50 and 100 yd and both axes

published.source: Green Eye Tactical, "Comparative Study of Red Dot Sight Parallax" (2017), as transcribed in a post on the accuratereloading.com optics forum (thread 7031016252), read 2026-11-17. Average deviation over all distances and testers.

published_parallax.verdict: The model sits below the published averages for three tube and micro sights. That study had human testers moving their heads, so its figures include more than the optics; this is a plausibility check, not a calibration.

published_brightness.what: Top daylight setting against the brightest background the class is specified for
published_brightness.published: Aimpoint CompM4 product sheet: dot visible against a background luminance of 0.1 to 55,000 lx (seen in a search summary on 2026-11-17, not in the document itself)
published_brightness.background_note: 55,000 lx on a 90 percent diffuse white surface: L = E * 0.9 / pi

click.what: Click value against the class figure
click.published_source: Aimpoint CompM4 user manual, section 1.1 Specification
